text:
Maya H.: Heads up — I'm doing a preflight playbook refresh for az14 (gpu-satellite). Goal: consolidate bootstrap checks, validation scripts, and a concise 'known issues' section for oncall handoff. Planning to stage at /docs/runbooks/regions/az14-preflight.md. Looking for anything we regularly tripped on (network, drivers, quota, cost).
Ravi K.: SGTM. Please include explicit driver/kernel checks. Example snippet we use:```bash
# validate GPU driver
modprobe nvidia || echo 'no nvidia module'
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
```
Jonah P.: Also add a pod eviction/taint validation step. We've seen kv-cache corruption when pods roll unexpectedly during warmup. Quick one-liner to find non-daemonset GPU pods:```bash
kubectl get pods -A -o custom-columns='NAMESPACE:metadata.namespace,NAME:metadata.name,NODE:spec.nodeName,CONT:spec.containers[*].name' | grep gpu
```
Anna S.: Add a short cost guidance bullet: recommended instance families (g5, a10/ga100 where applicable), on-demand vs reserved delta, and an example monthly estimate for a 10-GPU pool. Link to cost sheet: https://intranet.redwood/costs/region-az14 (placeholder).
ops-bot: runbook-draft-bot created a draft at /docs/runbooks/regions/az14-preflight.md (branch: runbook/az14-preflight).
Liam T.: We should include a quick latency smoke test to validate cold-start and long-seq behaviour. Suggest:```bash
./scripts/latency_check.sh --model rwd-small --seq 256 --iter 5 --warmup 2
# expect <120ms/token at steady state for dedicated pool
```
Maya H.: Good catches. I'll add a short "preflight checklist" section with those commands and a validation matrix (driver, kernel, MTU, NAT, ENI quotas, iptables conntracks). Draft checklist sample:
```
- check kernel + nvidia driver
- check container runtime compatibility (nvidia-container-runtime)
- validate MTU (1432 vs 1500) on pod interface
- confirm ENI / IP quota >= expected pods * 1.2
- verify route tables for TGW peering if cross-region access needed
- run latency_check.sh and record baseline
```
Ravi K.: Note on MTU: some HPC NICs prefer 1432, which caused fragmented GRPC frames in a previous deploy. Add remediation commands to fix the node-level MTU and restart kube-proxy. Also add a checkbox to verify nvidia driver >= 535 for our recommended AMIs.
Jonah P.: Add a note about spot/preemptible eviction handling: set pod disruption budgets, pre-stop hooks to flush KV cache, and a small integration test to simulate eviction.
Anna S.: I will add the cost bullets and a short paragraph about Dedicated reserved capacity vs burst (how to size commit to avoid overruns). Also flag the billing alert thresholds (e.g., 70/90/100% of committed).
Maya H.: I'll add a "known issues" section with: MTU fragmentation (fix steps), intermittent route missing on TGW (fix: add missing route to subnet), driver mismatch (AMIs pinned), and a short troubleshooting flowchart.
Ravi K.: One more: include automatic quota checks we can run as part of onboarding. Something like:
```bash
aws ec2 describe-account-attributes --attribute-names max-instances
# and check ENI/ip allocation per AZ
```
Jonah P.: Can someone review before EOD so we can fold into the next oncall handoff? @Anna S. @Ravi K. :eyes:
Anna S.: I'll review after stand, will add cost examples and verify the billing thresholds. :thumbsup:
Maya H.: Created PR: https://git.internal/repos/runbooks/pulls/42 — summary + checklist + smoke tests. Please add inline comments. :shipit:
ops-bot: CI / lint: runbook lint passed, spellcheck warnings (2) — see CI job 721.
Liam T.: Quick ask: add a short 'how to measure baseline' section with commands to capture GPU utilization + network p95 during a 5-min load. That helped us catch a noisy neighbor in az9.
Maya H.: Will add that. Thanks everyone, I'll iterate on the PR and aim to merge tomorrow morning so oncall has a fresh doc before the AZ14 provisioning window.
